investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-17T00:59:24Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at the /v1/agents endpoint. Because the failure is shared across every sibling check with the exact same error message, the fault is localized to the swarm gateway layer upstream of the agent provisioning API, not to any individual check's logic.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST /api/agents call, which in turn proxies to this gateway. Because the gateway returned a connection-level error before any agent was provisioned, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) could be collected, causing all three checks to fail with code bad_gateway. The root cause is a shared upstream infrastructure dependency failure at the swarm gateway, not a defect in the eval runner or check contract logic. No suspect code changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to implicate a recent deployment.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Failure: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=739, max=300)
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 739 minutes old, exceeding the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness assertion; all three sibling public-website checks passed, confirming no broader site outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 739 minutes (~12.3 hours). The snapshot itself is structurally valid and sourced from github-actions (evidence: source="github-actions", hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true, featureCount=19), but its age violates the snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 assertion defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482. The root cause is a missed or failed scheduled workflow run that publishes the snapshot, not a problem with the eval runner, the public website, or the snapshot schema.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 739' — the sole violated assertion, directly observed in the eval result.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=739, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true, featureCount=19 — the snapshot is structurally complete and live-sourced but stale by 439 minutes.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed, including the /observability route returning HTTP 200 — the public website is reachable and the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness.
source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check is registered as required=false, statusImpact='informational' — this eval failure does not constitute a service outage by registry contract.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot failed silently or was skipped, leaving the previously published snapshot in place for 739+ minutes.
Second: The GitHub Actions workflow was disabled, paused, or its schedule trigger was removed or misconfigured, preventing any run from occurring within the freshness window.
Third: The workflow ran but failed during the publish/deploy step (e.g., GitHub Pages deployment error), so the snapshot file on GitHub Pages was not updated even though the workflow was triggered.
Fourth: A GitHub Actions quota, rate limit, or runner availability issue caused the scheduled run to be queued but not executed within the expected window.

Fifth (lower confidence): A repository or Pages configuration change caused the snapshot to be published to a different path or URL, leaving the canonical URL stale — however, the snapshot URL in evidence matches the registered snapshotUrl, making this less likely.
